title: Accelerated Multipromoter Discovery for Alumina‑Supported Pt Catalysts in Non‑oxidative Propane Dehydrogenation via Iterative Design‑of‑Experiments
abstract:
The present disclosure provides a data‑efficient methodology for the rapid identification of effective promoter combinations that enhance the performance and lifetime of industrial catalysts. The approach integrates an iterative design‑of‑experiments (DoE) framework with a parallelized high‑throughput testing protocol to explore a multipromoter design space while limiting the total number of experiments to fewer than one hundred within a matter of weeks. By systematically planning measurement batches and adapting the experimental design based on interim results, the method enables quantitative assessment of both positive and negative influences of individual promoters on reaction yield and catalyst deactivation.  

Applied to the non‑oxidative dehydrogenation of propane to propylene over a platinum catalyst supported on alumina, the disclosed strategy identified a competitive promoter chemistry that improves catalytic activity and stability. The disclosed iterative DoE process serves as a generalizable concept for hypothesis validation and insight‑driven refinement of catalyst design spaces, offering a scalable route to accelerate the discovery of multipromoter systems beyond the limited set currently employed in empirical catalyst development.
